title: The AI race
description: Who shipped what, and when. Frontier labs and the infrastructure underneath them, from the founding of OpenAI to the current generation of models.

entities.name: OpenAI
entities.blurb: Founded as a non-profit research lab, restructured under a capped-profit arm in 2019. Put generative AI in front of the public with ChatGPT.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.blurb: Started by former OpenAI research leadership. Built Claude, and published the Constitutional AI and interpretability work the field now builds on.

entities.name: Google DeepMind
entities.blurb: DeepMind, acquired by Google in 2014 and merged with Google Brain in 2023. Produced the Transformer paper, AlphaGo and AlphaFold before Gemini.

entities.name: Meta AI
entities.blurb: FAIR under Yann LeCun, then the Llama family — the models that made open weights a serious competitive position rather than a compromise.

entities.name: Mistral AI
entities.blurb: Paris-based, founded by ex-DeepMind and ex-Meta researchers. Europe's frontier lab, built on small efficient models and open weights.

entities.name: xAI
entities.blurb: Elon Musk's lab, launched a year after he left OpenAI's board. Grok ships tightly coupled to X.

entities.name: Nvidia
entities.blurb: Not a lab, but the reason the labs can train anything. CUDA and the datacentre GPU line are the substrate the whole race runs on.

entities.name: Hugging Face
entities.blurb: The commons. Transformers, the model hub and the datasets that made open research distributable.

events.title: OpenAI founded
events.summary: Announced as a non-profit research company with a $1bn funding commitment, explicitly framed around distributing the benefits of AI rather than concentrating them.

events.title: GPT-1
events.summary: Generative pre-training on unlabelled text, then fine-tuning per task. The paper that established the recipe every model here still follows.

events.title: GPT-2
events.summary: Withheld at full size on misuse grounds, which set off the first real argument about staged release. The full model followed nine months later.

events.title: Microsoft invests $1bn
events.summary: Azure becomes OpenAI's exclusive compute provider. The template for every lab-and-hyperscaler pairing that followed.

events.title: GPT-3 and the API
events.summary: 175 billion parameters, and the first time few-shot prompting alone was enough to be useful. Shipped as an API rather than weights, which set the commercial pattern.

events.title: DALL·E
events.summary: Text-to-image from the same transformer recipe, and the first broad signal that generative models were not going to stay inside text.

events.title: ChatGPT
events.summary: A research preview wrapped around GPT-3.5 that reached a hundred million users in two months. The moment the field stopped being an industry story.

events.title: GPT-4
events.summary: Multimodal input and a large jump on professional benchmarks, published with no architecture or training details at all — the point where frontier work went closed.

events.title: Altman removed, then reinstated
events.summary: The board dismissed its CEO on a Friday; almost all staff threatened to leave, and he was back within five days. The governance structure did not survive the week.

events.title: Sora
events.summary: Minute-long video from text, shown well before anyone could use it. Set the expectation that video was the next modality to fall.

events.title: GPT-4o
events.summary: One model handling text, vision and audio end to end, at roughly half the price and twice the speed of GPT-4 Turbo. Native voice with conversational latency.

events.title: o1 — reasoning at inference time
events.summary: Spends compute thinking before answering rather than only at training time. Opened a second scaling axis the whole field moved onto within a year.

events.title: GPT-5
events.summary: Reasoning folded into the default model with automatic routing, rather than sold as a separate mode the user has to choose.

events.title: Anthropic emerges with $124m
events.summary: Founded by Dario and Daniela Amodei with a group who left OpenAI, around a bet that steerability and interpretability are the research problem, not a bolt-on.

events.title: Constitutional AI
events.summary: Training a model to critique and revise its own output against a written set of principles, cutting how much human feedback is needed to make it harmless.

events.title: Claude
events.summary: Launched the same day as GPT-4, positioned on being steerable and harder to push into harmful output rather than on raw capability.

events.title: Claude 2
events.summary: A 100k-token context window when rivals offered a fraction of it, which made long-document work the first thing Claude was reached for.

events.title: Claude 3 family
events.summary: Haiku, Sonnet and Opus as one release across three price points — the tiering approach every lab now copies. Opus took the benchmark lead from GPT-4.

events.title: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
events.summary: The mid-tier model beating the previous flagship, at a fifth of the price. Coding performance made it the default for engineering work.

events.title: Model Context Protocol
events.summary: An open standard for connecting models to tools and data, given away rather than kept proprietary. Adopted across the industry within a year.

events.title: Claude 4
events.summary: Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, built for agents that run for hours rather than turns. Claude Code shipped alongside as the reference case.

events.title: Claude Sonnet 5
events.summary: Frontier performance in the mid tier — coding, agents and professional work at a price meant for volume rather than demonstrations.

events.title: Claude Opus 5
events.summary: A step change for the Opus tier, aimed at long-running agents and sustained coding work rather than single answers.

events.title: DeepMind founded
events.summary: Hassabis, Legg and Suleyman set out to 'solve intelligence, and then use it to solve everything else' — a framing the field still argues about.

events.title: Google acquires DeepMind
events.summary: Around $500m, with an internal ethics board as a condition. Put frontier research inside a hyperscaler years before anyone else managed it.

events.title: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
events.summary: 4–1 at Go, a decade before anyone expected it. The result that convinced the public deep learning was not incremental.

events.title: Attention Is All You Need
events.summary: The Transformer, published by Google Brain. Every model on this page descends from this paper, including those built by its authors' later companies.

events.title: AlphaFold 2 solves CASP14
events.summary: Protein structure prediction at experimental accuracy, closing a fifty-year problem in biology and later sharing a Nobel Prize.

events.title: Brain and DeepMind merge
events.summary: Google folded its two research organisations into one under Hassabis, five months after ChatGPT made the internal competition untenable.

events.title: Gemini 1.0
events.summary: Natively multimodal from pre-training rather than stitched together afterwards, shipped in Nano, Pro and Ultra sizes.

events.title: Gemini 1.5 Pro — one million tokens
events.summary: A context window an order of magnitude beyond anyone else, which turned 'can it read my whole codebase' from a workaround into a feature.

events.title: Gemini 2.5 Pro
events.summary: Reasoning built into the base model, and the point where Google's frontier offering was consistently competitive rather than catching up.

events.title: Gemini 3 Pro
events.summary: The third generation, with Deep Think and Flash variants following within a month — a release cadence closer to weeks than years.

events.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro
events.summary: An incremental frontier update, shipped four months after 3 Pro. By this point point releases arrive faster than most teams can evaluate them.

events.title: FAIR founded under Yann LeCun
events.summary: Facebook AI Research set up as an open publishing lab, a commitment that later made the Llama releases consistent rather than surprising.

events.title: PyTorch
events.summary: Eager execution and a Python-native feel took research off TensorFlow within about three years. Most models here were trained in it.

events.title: LLaMA
events.summary: Released to researchers, then leaked within a week. The leak seeded the entire local-model ecosystem and forced the open-weights question into the open.

events.title: Llama 2 — open weights, commercial use
events.summary: Deliberately licensed for commercial use, turning the leak into a strategy. Made open weights a competitive position rather than a concession.

events.title: Llama 3.1 405B
events.summary: The first open-weights model credibly compared with closed frontier models, and the strongest form of the argument that the gap was closing.

events.title: Llama 4
events.summary: A natively multimodal mixture-of-experts generation, released into a market where open weights had stopped being unusual.

events.title: Mistral founded with a €105m seed
events.summary: Ex-DeepMind and ex-Meta researchers raised Europe's largest seed round four weeks after incorporating, on a deck and a track record.

events.title: Mistral 7B
events.summary: Beat Llama 2 13B at half the size, released under Apache 2.0 via a bare magnet link. Made 'small and efficient' a serious position.

events.title: Mixtral 8x7B
events.summary: A sparse mixture-of-experts with open weights, matching much larger dense models while only activating a fraction of them per token.

events.title: Mistral Large and the Microsoft deal
events.summary: A closed flagship alongside the open models, distributed on Azure — the point where Europe's open-source champion took a hyperscaler partner.

events.title: xAI founded
events.summary: Musk launched a rival lab five years after leaving OpenAI's board, staffed largely from DeepMind, OpenAI and Google.

events.title: Grok
events.summary: Announced with live access to X as its distinguishing feature — real-time data as the moat rather than raw capability.

events.title: Grok-1 weights released
events.summary: A 314-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts published under Apache 2.0, the largest open-weights release at the time.

events.title: Grok 3
events.summary: Trained on the Colossus cluster xAI built in Memphis in months rather than years — the clearest demonstration that compute could be bought as speed.

events.title: CUDA
events.summary: General-purpose programming on GPUs, shipped years before deep learning needed it. The lock-in that every competitor still cannot dislodge.

events.title: A100
events.summary: The Ampere datacentre part that GPT-3 and most of the following generation were trained on. Became the unit of account for compute.

events.title: H100
events.summary: Hopper, with a transformer engine built for exactly this workload. Supply of it, not ideas, became the binding constraint on frontier training.

events.title: Nvidia passes $1tn
events.summary: Six months after ChatGPT, the market repriced the supplier rather than the labs — the first hard financial read on where the value was accruing.

events.title: Blackwell
events.summary: The generation after Hopper, announced with the datacentre treated as the unit of design rather than the chip.

events.title: Transformers library
events.summary: Started as a PyTorch port of BERT and became the default way to load a model. Reduced 'use this architecture' to a single line.

events.title: The Model Hub
events.summary: Hosting for weights and datasets with versioning, which made distributing an open model a push rather than a project.

events.title: BLOOM
events.summary: A 176-billion-parameter multilingual model trained in the open by a thousand researchers, on public French supercomputing time.

events.title: $235m at a $4.5bn valuation
events.summary: Google, Amazon, Nvidia and Salesforce all invested in the same round — the commons funded by everyone competing on top of it.
